To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microdomains can be generated in multicomponent biomembranes by (i) critical fluctuations close to a critical point, (ii) the formation of multiple domains on curved surfaces, (iii) the formation of microemulsions in two dimensions, and (iv) non-equilibrium mechanisms such as the pinning of domains by the cytoplasm and domain recycling.

(i) the critical cluster mechanism is the only equilibrium mechanism that can generate micro- or nanodomains in lipid bilayers in the thermodynamic equilibrium, (ii) the effect of linactant molecules is an equilibrium mechanism that can lead to the formation of two-dimensional microemulsion droplets, and (iii), the pinning effects are a non-equilibrium mechanism, which leads to the formation of micro- or nanodomain patterns in lipid bilayers.

(i) critical cluster formation close to phase transitions, curvature-composition coupling and membrane recycling are the most important mechanisms that can generate nanodomains in membranes, (ii) the size of nanodomains can be estimated by a simple scaling law, which is derived from the theory of phase separation, and (iii), the size distribution of nanodomains depends on their formation mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the physical mechanisms of micro- (10-100 nm) and nanodomains (1-10 nm) in multicomponent biomembranes.
the physical mechanisms of domain formation in multicomputent biomembranes.
the physical mechanisms of micro- or nanodomain formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the physical mechanisms of micro- or nanodomain formation are not well understood, but the field has made significant progress in the last 10 years, and there are good chances that this progress will continue.
the mechanisms discussed in this article, as well as others not discussed here, can all be realized in principle.
micro- and nanoscale domains can be generated by a number of physical mechanisms that do not require direct protein-lipid or protein-protein interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of lipid micro- and nanoclusters in biomembranes can be understood in terms of the theory of phase separation and critical phenomena.
the formation of micro- and nano-domains is a very complex process.
we are trying to find the right physical mechanisms for the formation of lipid domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
micro- and nanoscale lipid domain formation is a very general phenomenon in multicomponent biomembranes and can be induced by various physical mechanisms.
a variety of different physical mechanisms can generate micro- or nanodomains in lipid membranes.
a variety of physical effects can lead to the formation of microdomains.
